source.title: Minimal sufficient views: A DNN model making predictions with more evidence has higher accuracy
source.authors: Keisuke Kawano; Takuro Kutsuna; Keisuke Sano

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether a measured network property—the estimated number of minimal sufficient views—tracks prediction accuracy, using a different measure from the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper measures MSV counts and prediction accuracy, but does not test the specific conditions or measures named in V1–V8. MSV counts are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The study tests whether estimated minimal sufficient view counts correlate with prediction accuracy. It neither tests nor uses any specific finding in V1–V8. In particular, image-region masking is not weight-perturbation sharpness (V7) or removal of memorized training examples followed by retraining (V8).
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors report associations between estimated MSV counts and prediction accuracy within and across models, and propose mean MSV count for model selection without labels. These are observational associations; they do not establish that increasing the evidence count causes improved generalization.
record.recipe_differences: Measures estimated minimal sufficient views and their association with prediction accuracy; it does not reproduce the random-label, width, optimizer, batch-size, regularization, sharpness, or memorized-example methods in the listed originals.
record.method_sensitivity: The estimated MSVs and their counts depend on the splitting method, β, random seed, and masking baseline. The reported count-accuracy relationship is described as stable across tested β values, seeds, and splitting methods; Table 2 reports accuracy increasing with count across masking baselines.

fits_no_version.finding: ResNet-101 accuracy generally rises across ImageNet validation groups with more estimated MSVs, from 0.538 for one MSV to 0.937 for at least ten. Alternative masking baselines preserve the broad association, with fluctuations among higher-count bins.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within an image classifier, predictions supported by more estimated disjoint sufficient image regions tend to be more accurate.

fits_no_version.finding: Mean MSV count has rank correlations with accuracy of 0.93 across ImageNet models, 0.58 across CIFAR-100-finetuned models, and 0.92 across the ImageNet-C evaluation including ResNet-50 and ViT_B_16.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Mean estimated MSV count is associated with image-classification accuracy across tested models and corruption settings.

record.peer_reviewed: Neural Networks, Elsevier; author accepted manuscript states final version published in Neural Networks
record.problems: The paper studies image classification and MSV count, not the specific claim versions' interventions or measures. Some cross-model results and correlations are presented in figures; the mean-score confidence intervals are described as bootstrap ranges but their numeric endpoints are not given in the text. MSV estimates depend on several hyperparameters.
record.rows_left_out: Tables 2–4 report additional per-count accuracies for masking baselines, SLIC seeds, and splitting methods. They are omitted here to keep the record focused on the primary per-count result and reported cross-model/dataset associations; the paper states these comparisons preserve the accuracy-count relationship. Figure 10 also reports correlations for β=4–32; those correlations are omitted because the text summarizes them as high regardless of β.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, chance-level random-label held-out accuracy, and coexistence with natural-label generalization under the same recipe.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected training, local connectivity, learned sparsity, and convolution-derived initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimization and the effects of tuning, weight decay, or optimizer switching.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that reduce their generalization penalty.
Dropout interventions and their dependence on dataset size, dropout strength, augmentation, or weight decay.
Magnitude-scaled weight perturbations, training–test gaps at similarly low training loss, and comparisons with norm- and margin-based generalization measures.
Identifying memorized training examples, removing them, and comparing retraining accuracy with matched random removals.

record.verdict_notes: None of the listed versions receives a verdict. The cited originals provide background rather than tested premises. States are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8; this does not dispute the reported MSV associations.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Large-batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets and recipe changes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons with norm- or margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.

rows.uncertainty: 1%-99% percentile range of bootstrap mean values shown; numeric interval not stated
rows.note: Authors state a clear relationship across the model groups.
rows.check: Correlation 0.93 is correct. This compares MSV counts with validation accuracy across heterogeneous pretrained architectures, not any listed version.

rows.subject: TorchVision ImageNet-trained models finetuned on CIFAR-100
rows.operation_detail: Finetuned with SGD for 200 epochs; evaluated mean MSV count against accuracy.
rows.measure: Rank correlation between mean MSV count and accuracy
rows.uncertainty: 1%-99% bootstrap confidence intervals shown; numeric interval not stated
rows.note: Figure reports the correlation; text says MSV count had higher correlation than other scores.
rows.check: Correlation 0.58 is correct. Models were selected by their best validation accuracy during finetuning. The correlation tests no listed version.

rows.subject: ResNet50

rows.note: Text says increasing distortion further reduces MSV count and accuracy.
rows.check: Subject is incomplete: Figure 9 includes both ResNet-50 and ViT_B_16. The reported 0.92 correlation describes the combined plotted evaluation, not a stated ResNet-50-only correlation. No listed version is measured.
